title: Termwise complex differentiation on a disc under summable derivative bounds
statement: Let $I$ be any index set, let $r>0$, and put $D=\{z\in\mathbf C:|z|<r\}$, using [def-weil-complex-absolute-value]. Let $g_i,g_i^{\prime}:\mathbf C\to\mathbf C$ for $i\in I$, and $u:I\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ with $\sum_i u_i<\infty$. Suppose $g_i$ has ordinary complex derivative $g_i^{\prime}(z)$ at every $z\in D$, that $|g_i^{\prime}(z)|\leq u_i$ for all $i$ and $z\in D$, and that $(g_i(0))_{i\in I}$ is summable. Then $G(z)=\sum_i g_i(z)$ has ordinary complex derivative $\sum_i g_i^{\prime}(z)$ at every $z\in D$. All sums mean limits of finite subsums, and ordinary derivative is the limit of the complex difference quotient.
